Unit 6: Data & Information

SL curriculum overview and structured learning plan.

Introduction

How do we structure data so it tells the truth?

This unit explores Data Integrity and Relational Databases. You will learn to move beyond messy 'flat files' to structured Entities linked by Keys. The goal is to design systems that reduce redundancy (repetition) and ensure consistency.

You'll start by deconstructing messy data into Normalized tables (1NF, 2NF, 3NF). Then you'll model these structures using ERD Diagrams, and finally, learn the language of databases — SQL — to query and manipulate the data.

The Relational Model

Modern databases store data in related tables, not single spreadsheet files.

  • Entity (Table): A collection of data about one thing (e.g., "Students").
  • Tuple (Row): A single record (e.g., "John Doe").
  • Attribute (Column): A specific piece of data (e.g., "DateOfBirth").
  • Primary Key: A unique ID that identifies a record.
  • Foreign Key: A link to a Primary Key in another table.
Normalization

Normalization is a 3-step mathematical process to organize data and reduce redundancy:

  • 1NF: Atomic Data (no lists in cells) + Unique Rows.
  • 2NF: 1NF + No Partial Dependencies (all attributes depend on the WHOLE key).
  • 3NF: 2NF + No Transitive Dependencies (attributes depend ONLY on the key).
ERD Diagrams

We visualize database schemas using Entity Relationship Diagrams.

  • Entity: Represented by a rectangle.
  • Attribute: Ovals or listed inside.
  • Relationships: Lines connecting entities with Cardinality (1:1, 1:Many, Many:Many).
SQL (Declarative Programming)

SQL is not procedural (how to do it), it is declarative (what you want). You just ask the database:

  • DDL (Data Definition): CREATE, DROP tables.
  • DML (Data Manipulation): SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE.
Key Terminology
TermDefinition
Database An organized collection of data, generally stored and accessed electronically from a computer system.
Relational Database A type of database that stores and provides access to data points that are related to one another.
Primary Key A specific choice of a minimal set of attributes (columns) that uniquely specify a tuple (row) in a relation (table).
Foreign Key A field (or collection of fields) in one table that refers to the PRIMARY KEY in another table.
Normalization The process of organizing data in a database to reduce redundancy and improve data integrity.
Schema The skeleton structure that represents the logical configuration of all or part of a relational database.
Cardinality Refers to the uniqueness of data values contained in a column (e.g., One-to-One, One-to-Many).
SQL Structured Query Language. A domain-specific language used in programming for managing data held in a relational database management system.
DDL Data Definition Language. The subset of SQL used to define the data structures (e.g., CREATE TABLE).
DML Data Manipulation Language. The subset of SQL used to manage data (e.g., SELECT, INSERT).
